[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine whole numbers: 10 + 15 − 4 = 21

Combine fractions: 2/3 + 1/3 − 1/6

⇒ 1 − 1/6 = 5/6

Total = 21 + 5/6 = 21 5/6

**∴ The correct answer is 21 5/6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 10 2/3 + 15 1/3 − 4 1/6

Method: Convert mixed fractions to improper fractions and solve using LCM.

⇒ (32/3) + (46/3) − (25/6)

⇒ (32 × 2 / 6) + (46 × 2 / 6) − (25/6)

⇒ (64/6) + (92/6) − (25/6)

⇒ (64 + 92 − 25) / 6

⇒ 131 / 6

⇒ 21 5/6

**∴ The correct answer is 21 5/6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixed Fraction Conversion

A b/c is converted to improper fraction as (A × c + b) / c.

LCM Method

To add or subtract fractions with different denominators, find the Least Common Multiple of the denominators to make them like fractions.

BODMAS in Fractions

Perform operations in the order of Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.
